scope: One rerun of the summarized-natural-language arm on the same 150 cases, with the same source sentence summaries and two-stage questions. Replace numerical context and earlier probabilities with explicit qualitative interpretations, not percentages in sentences. All cases are previously examined development/regression cases; 149 deterministic outcomes are scoreable.

response_policy.validation: Reuse strict concrete model, answer type, probability and identical-request retry checks. Preserve every response and rejection. No correctness-based retries.

inputs: Reference immutable representation_cases/raw_states/summaries/questions/outcomes files. No new prices, sources or independently invented analyst consensus. Monetary values and dates remain literal. Exact +/-1% target boundaries remain literal to preserve the evaluator. Source financial percentage values remain source facts, with contextual explanations where the text explicitly establishes a revenue-growth or margin meaning. Market evidence, the reference forecast and earlier Jev probabilities are rendered qualitatively without numerical probabilities.
movement_words: For a historical h-session return compute z=abs(return)/(daily_volatility_20*sqrt(h)) in code. Below0.25=very small; [0.25,0.75)=modest; [0.75,1.5)=substantial; >=1.5=strong. Always preserve rise/fall. If volatility is unavailable, use neutral rise/fall wording without a magnitude adjective. These are fixed presentation categories, not statistical significance or future-return predictions.
relative_words: Compare stock-minus-SPY return with sqrt(stock_daily_variance+SPY_daily_variance)*sqrt(h). Use the same qualitative magnitude bins and preserve outperformance/underperformance. This simple display scale omits covariance and is not an alpha or significance estimate.
volatility_words: Daily variability below1%=relatively subdued; [1%,2%)=moderate; [2%,4%)=elevated; >=4%=very high. Do not confuse variability with expected appreciation. Display only the qualitative words in Jev state.
evidence_words: Earlier yes probabilities: <=0.05 almost no support; (0.05,0.20] little support; (0.20,0.40) weak support leaning against; [0.40,0.60] unresolved; (0.60,0.80) moderate support; [0.80,0.95) strong support; >=0.95 very strong support. These are attributed model judgments, not established facts. Unknown means insufficient evidence and never no effect or flat.
choice_words: Summarize the leading business interpretation using the above strength bins and mention other interpretations with probability>=0.10 as plausible/weak alternatives. Explicitly preserve the difference between missing evidence and unchanged economics. A separate model-reported confidence is described as low/limited/fairly confident/high/very high by fixed bins, not treated as a return probability.
reference_words: Describe the training-only market reference's preferred direction and strength in words, with alternatives. Do not turn its up preference into a fact, recommendation or guaranteed continuation.
comparisons: Compare new end-to-end forecasts against saved raw JSON, percentage descriptions, earlier summarized prose, single-call and market-only/prior/constants. Report all150 and original chronological subgroups, Brier, full-coverage accuracy, balanced accuracy, class confusions, coverage, intermediate judgment distributions and token lengths. Paired calendar-month bootstrap 5000 draws seed2718. No statistical refit or selection loop.
freeze: Freeze all source-file hashes, protocol, qualitative input texts and code before smoke. Smoke uses first three training cases and checks transport/schema only. Run one fixed qualitative transformation, report even if worse. No post-score wording adjustments.
preservation: Keep all new qualitative_ records inside existing folders; do not modify representation_ or earlier experiment files. Save a full before/after trace for the previously discussed Apple case.
